en: Amr al-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: A group of Jews asked permission to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: "Death be upon you (as-Samu alaykum)." Aisha said: "Rather, upon you be death and the curse!" The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O Aisha, indeed Allah loves gentleness in all matters." She said: "Did you not hear what they said?" He said: "I already said: And upon you."

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that he said: "So say: And upon you (wa alayk)."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya ibn Yahya's; Yahya ibn Yahya said: informed us, and the others said: Ismail—namely Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Dinar, that he heard Ibn Umar saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When the Jews greet you, one of them says: Death be upon you (as-Samu alaykum). So say: Upon you (alayk)."

Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us (H). And Yahya ibn Habib narrated to me: Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us; both said: Shu'bah narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is theirs; both said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas that the Companions of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): "Indeed, the People of the Book greet us with peace, so how should we respond to them?" He said: "Say: And upon you (wa alaykum)."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, he said: I heard Anas saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said (H). And Isma'il ibn Salim narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us: Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr informed us, from his grandfather Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "When the People of the Book greet you with peace, say: And upon you (wa alaykum)."

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us, they said: Ismail—namely Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The rights of a Muslim upon a Muslim are six." It was said: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "When you meet him, greet him with peace; when he invites you, respond to him; when he seeks your advice, give him sincere advice; when he sneezes and praises Allah, pray for mercy upon him; when he falls ill, visit him; and when he dies, follow his funeral."

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The rights of a Muslim upon a Muslim are five" (H). And Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Five things are obligatory for a Muslim toward his brother: returning the greeting of peace, responding to the one who sneezes, accepting the invitation, visiting the sick, and following funerals." Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar used to narrate this hadith as mursal from al-Zuhri, and he once connected its chain from Ibn al-Musayyab from Abu Hurayrah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Affan narrated to us: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us: Uthman ibn Hakim narrated to us, from Ishaq ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, from his father, who said: Abu Talhah said: We were sitting in the courtyards conversing when the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came and stood over us, saying: "Why do you sit in the pathways? Avoid sitting in the pathways." We said: "We are only sitting for no harm; we sat to remind one another and converse." He said: "If you must, then give it its right: lowering the gaze, returning greetings of peace, and good speech."

Uqbah ibn Mukram narrated to me: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj (H). And Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to me: Rawh narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Ziyad informed me that Thabit, the freed slave of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "The rider should greet the pedestrian with peace, the pedestrian should greet the one who is seated, and the smaller group should greet the larger group."
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Abd al-A'la informed us; and Ishaq said: Waki' informed us: Sufyan narrated to us; both from Yunus with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us (H). And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ismail ibn Ulayyah narrated to us; both from Yunus (H). And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Hushaym narrated to us: Yunus informed us, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Zur'ah, from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about an accidental glance, and he commanded me to avert my gaze.

Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "If a man peeks in on you without permission and you flick a small pebble at him and put out his eye, there is no blame upon you."

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), who said: "Whoever peeks into the house of people without their permission, it becomes permissible for them to put out his eye."

Yahya ibn Yahya, Abu Kamil Fudayl ibn Husayn, and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya and Abu Kamil's; Yahya said: informed us, and the other two said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from Anas ibn Malik, that a man peeked into one of the rooms of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so he stood up toward him with an arrow-blade or arrow-blades. It is as if I am looking at the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) trying to take him by surprise so as to stab him.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Amr al-Naqid, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us (H). And Abu Kamil al-Jahdari narrated to us: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us; both from al-Zuhri, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), similar to the hadith of al-Layth and Yunus.

And Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi informed him that a man peeked through a hole in the door of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had an iron comb with which he was combing his hair. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: "If I had known you were looking, I would have stabbed you in the eye with it. Allah only ordained seeking permission because of the sight."

Yahya ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us, they said: al-Layth informed us—and the wording is Yahya's (H). And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi informed him that a man peeked through a hole in the door of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had an iron comb with which he was scratching his head. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw him, he said: "If I had known you were looking at me, I would have stabbed you in the eye with it." And the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Seeking permission was only ordained because of the sight."

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and Abu Amir al-Aqadi narrated to us (H). And Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to me (H). And Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us; all of them from Shu'bah, with this chain of narration. And in their hadith: as if he disliked that.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr's; Yahya said: informed us, and Abu Bakr said: Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I asked permission to enter upon the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), and he said: "Who is this?" I said: "Me." So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Me, me!"

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I came to the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and called out. The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Who is this?" I said: "Me." He said: So he came out saying: "Me, me!"

And Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Aban narrated it to us: Ali ibn Hashim narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, with this chain of narration, except that he said: He said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)?" He said: "Yes, so do not be a punishment upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), O Ibn al-Khattab." And he did not mention Umar's saying: "Glory be to Allah," and what follows it.

Husayn ibn Hurayth Abu Ammar narrated to us: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us: Talhah ibn Yahya informed us, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: Abu Musa came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "Peace be upon you, this is Abd Allah ibn Qays." But he did not give him permission. So he said: "Peace be upon you, this is Abu Musa. Peace be upon you, this is al-Ash'ari." Then he turned away. Umar said: "Bring him back to me, bring him back to me!" So he came, and Umar said: "O Abu Musa, what turned you back? We were busy." He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "Seeking permission is three times; if permission is granted to you, enter, otherwise go back." Umar said: "You must bring me proof for this, or else I shall do such-and-such to you!" So Abu Musa left. Umar said: "If he finds proof, you will find him by the pulpit this evening, and if he does not find proof, you will not find him." When evening came, they found him. Umar said: "O Abu Musa, what do you say? Have you found proof?" He said: "Yes, Ubayy ibn Ka'b." Umar said: "A trustworthy witness." Umar said: "O Abu al-Tufayl, what is this man saying?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say that, O Ibn al-Khattab, so do not be a punishment upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace)." Umar said: "Glory be to Allah! I only heard something and wanted to verify it."

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us (H). And Husayn ibn Hurayth narrated to us: al-Nadr—meaning Ibn Shumayl—narrated to us; both said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, with this chain of narration, the like of it, and in the hadith of al-Nadr he did not mention: "striking deals in the markets distracted me from it."

And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Ata' narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, that Abu Musa asked permission to enter upon Umar three times, and finding him busy, as it seemed, he returned. Umar said: "Did you not hear the voice of Abd Allah ibn Qays? Give him permission." So he was called, and Umar said: "What made you do what you did?" He said: "We were commanded to do this." Umar said: "You must bring proof for this or I will surely do something to you." So he went out and proceeded to a gathering of the Ansar, and they said: "None shall testify for you on this except the youngest of us." So Abu Sa'id stood up and said: "We were commanded to do this." Thereupon Umar said: "This matter from the command of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) remained hidden from me; striking deals in the markets distracted me from it."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Maslamah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id (H). And Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Khirash narrated to us: Shababah narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Jurayri and Sa'id ibn Yazid, both from Abu Nadrah; they said: We heard him narrating from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, in the meaning of the hadith of Bishr ibn Mufaddal from Abu Maslamah.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us: Bishr—meaning Ibn Mufaddal—narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that Abu Musa came to Umar's door and asked permission, and Umar said: "One." Then he asked permission a second time, and Umar said: "Two." Then he asked permission a third time, and Umar said: "Three." Then he left, so Umar followed him and brought him back, saying: "If this is something you learned by heart from the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), then well and good; otherwise, I shall make an example of you." Abu Sa'id said: So he came to us and said: "Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: Seeking permission is three times?" He said: So they began laughing. Abu Sa'id said: I said: "Your Muslim brother has come to you terrified, and you laugh? Go on, and I am your partner in this punishment." So he went to him and said: "Here is Abu Sa'id."

Abu al-Tahir narrated to me: Abd Allah ibn Wahb informed me: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, from Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj, that Busr ibn Sa'id narrated to him that he heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: We were in a gathering with Ubayy ibn Ka'b when Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came in anger, stood before us, and said: "I adjure you by Allah, did any of you hear the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: Seeking permission is three times; if permission is granted to you, enter, otherwise go back?" Ubayy said: "What is the matter?" He said: "I sought permission to enter upon Umar ibn al-Khattab yesterday three times, and permission was not given to me, so I went back. Then I came to him today, entered upon him, and informed him that I had come yesterday, greeted three times, and then left. He said: We heard you, but we were busy at the time; why didn't you keep seeking permission until permission was given to you? I said: I sought permission just as I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say. He said: By Allah, I will surely inflict pain on your back and stomach unless you bring someone who testifies for you to this!" Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: "By Allah, none shall stand with you except the youngest of us in age; stand up, O Abu Sa'id." So I stood up until I came to Umar and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say this."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id and Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, they said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Khusayfah, with this chain of narration. And Ibn Abi Umar added in his hadith: Abu Sa'id said: "So I stood up with him, went to Umar, and testified."

Amr ibn Muhammad ibn Bukayr al-Naqid narrated to me: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us: By Allah, Yazid ibn Khusayfah narrated to us, from Busr ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say: I was sitting in Medina in a gathering of the Ansar when Abu Musa came to us frightened or terrified. We said: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Umar sent for me to come to him, so I came to his door and greeted three times, but no one returned it to me, so I went back. He said: What prevented you from coming to us? I said: I came to you and greeted at your door three times, but they did not return it to me, so I went back, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: If one of you seeks permission three times and is not granted permission, let him go back. Umar said: Bring proof for this, or else I shall inflict pain on you! Thereupon Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: None shall stand with him except the youngest of the people. Abu Sa'id said: I said: I am the youngest of the people. He said: Then go with him."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us, they said: Waki' narrated to us (H). And Surayj ibn Yunus narrated to us: Hushaym narrated to us (H). And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir informed us (H). And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us; all of them from Ismail with this chain of narration. And in the hadith of none of them is the saying of the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) to al-Mughirah: "O my little son," except in the hadith of Yazid alone.
